brief.headline: Push for maker-direct pricing: they're 100% a trader carrying reseller margin — benchmark to a manufacturer and line up Manjushree as second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the maker's price or explain the reseller margin they're adding.
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to the market band of ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume (from the market ask: ₹0.55–1.20/pc band, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec).
priceAsk.basis: They're 100.0% a trader — their price carries a reseller margin. The market ask shows room down to ₹0.65–0.80 for items like a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap, so we want the manufacturer's price, not a middleman's markup.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask to stretch our payment window to 60 days — they already take 105 days to pay their own suppliers, so they can wait a bit longer for us.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving from 30 days to 45 days frees up ₹2.68 L of cash for us; a full push to 60 would free roughly double that.

brief.financialLeverage: They're on shaky ground — a money-health score of 2/10 and in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58). They keep only 2.8% as profit, so there's almost no cushion. But we're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr in sales — a big enough customer to matter. The smart play: don't squeeze price so hard you tip them over; instead, press for terms (they already take 105 days to pay suppliers, versus 57 days for similar firms) and qualify a second source fast.

evidence.point: They are entirely a trader — no manufacturing
They're in the financial grey zone
We are a meaningful customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹65.27 L spend = 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They pay their suppliers much slower than peers
They keep almost nothing as profit

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — with revenue of ₹2569.83 Cr and a health score of B (65/100). A robust second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, a credible alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead from public research (India-Pan, medium confidence) — verify and price before issuing RFQ.

risks: Their money-health is very poor (2/10) and they're in the grey distress zone — supply continuity is at risk if you push too hard or if their finances worsen.
They have pending legal case(s) flagged — check what those are before locking in a long-term commitment.
They're entirely a trader with no manufacturing — if their upstream maker has a problem or cuts them off, we have no fallback through them.
Their profit margin is only 2.8% — a steep price cut could push them into losses and jeopardize our supply; focus the negotiation on payment terms and securing a second source instead.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we need to talk about two things: getting closer to the manufacturer's price since you're trading these items, and extending our payment window to 60 days — you already take 105 days with your suppliers, so it's only fair.
